aboutMore: i work part time at a party supply store (balloon arches, mostly) so i can afford the $20 bracket fees, and about once a month i drive 3 hours to a regional with my dad in the passenger seat holding a bag of saltines. my little cousin maya is 9 and mains jigglypuff and she has beaten me in friendlies. i host friday friendlies in the basement and my mom brings out orange slices at halftime. i lose in winners semis a lot. i am working on it. i am extremely working on it.

blog.title: regional recap: 3 hours there, 3 hours back, 7 games in between
blog.body: left sacramento at 6:10 am. dad drove, i held the saltines. 3 hours to fresno, 2 gas station stops, 1 gas station burrito i regret less than the match. the venue was freezing, they always are, so i used all 4 hand warmers: one per pocket, two for the thumbs. i packed the whole setup, yes including the CRT, i'm not an animal. won my first set 3-0. won the second 3-1. then winners semis and i drew dale, the marth main from stockton who teaches middle school band. he beat me 3-1 and said 'good game, sorry!' after every stock. he MEANS it. that's the worst part. i went to losers and lost 3-2 in a last-hit game i will think about in the shower until november. final place: 17th. dad said 'that's more than most.' i said 'it's out of 40.' he said 'then it's still more than most.' he's the only coach i've ever needed. we got home at 1 am. mom left a plate on the counter with a note: 'positive!' and a smiley face.

blog.title: balloon arches: how i pay for 20XX
blog.body: people ask how i afford a hobby where every event costs $20 to enter, plus gas, plus the gas station burrito. the answer is balloons. i work tuesdays, thursdays and saturdays at a party supply place called Fiesta Barn. i blow up balloons. i have built 31 arches. one arch is one bracket entry. i think in arches now. a regional is two arches. a major is a whole wedding. i can tie a balloon dog in 11 seconds and my thumbs have never been stronger. here is the secret nobody tells you: balloon work is basically frame data. you have to know exactly how much pressure before it pops. too much and you're done. too little and the whole arch droops. i learned my release timing from a balloon fox. the ears were wrong. they are always wrong. a kid at a birthday party said it looked 'okay.' that's a nine star review.

blog.title: my cousin maya beat me (a statement, i'm fine)
blog.body: my cousin maya is nine and mains jigglypuff. i taught her everything: the buttons, how to shield, how to not mash. she picked jigglypuff because 'she's round.' sunday: friendlies. maya beat me 2 out of 5. i'd like to make three points. one, i was going easy. two, i wasn't. three, after the third match she said 'you're thinking too much, wes,' and my whole life flashed. she's right. i overthink every bracket set. maya doesn't think. she pushes the stick and hums. the lesson: in melee the kid with zero fear is a lot of fox. i'm trying to lose gracefully. today i shook her hand and said 'gg.' then i went to the garage and said 'gg' to the wall nine times at different volumes. on her suggestion i've taken up humming while i play. it's going badly. it's going well? she says it's going well. she's nine and she runs my whole life.

blog.title: the rules of friday friendlies (posted at the bottom of the basement stairs)
blog.body: 1. ports get inspected. i won't be sorry. 2. the winner doesn't pick the stage. the loser does. it's called mercy. 3. no johns. a john is any excuse. 'my controller drifted' is a john. 'the sun was in my eyes' in a basement is a double john. 4. you can say gg or you can say nothing. you cannot say 'that was lucky.' 5. my mom brings out orange slices at halftime. you eat one. it is not optional, she's watching from the stairs. 6. any kid under 12 gets first pick of character. i don't care if it's jigglypuff. 7. the last set of the night is always 2v2, where we all lose together. 8. nobody leaves until we've cleaned the controller ports as a group. rubbing alcohol and cotton swabs. it's very bonding. last week 11 people came, 4 of them new. one of them moved samus like water. i have never been so afraid or so happy.

survey.title: TOURNAMENT PLAYER SURVEY (copy/paste, brutally honest)
qa: name:
wes. tag is wavedash_wes. at the party store it's 'balloon guy.'
main:
fox. secondary: falco, for emotional days. my tertiary is 'cousin maya's jigglypuff,' for humility.
how far do you travel for a tournament:
3 hours to fresno, 2 to stockton, once 6 hours to a regional in l.a. where i lost first round to a guy named bob. bob was great.
pre-bracket meal:
7 almonds, a sleeve of saltines, a banana. i'm told it's 'not a meal.' it's a plan.
pre-bracket ritual:
i wash my hands 3 times, tape my thumbs, and say 'no johns' to the bathroom mirror. the mirror doesn't answer. that's good.
nerves, 1 to 10:
a 9 before the set. a 3 during. an 11 after, if i lost. it's a roller coaster that goes to the bathroom.
favorite thing about tournaments:
the hallway between sets where people trade tech. you walk in a stranger and someone shows you a trick and you walk out a friend.
least favorite thing:
the two hour wait to lose in six minutes.
your rival:
dale. marth. stockton. middle school band teacher. he says sorry after every stock. he is my favorite person and my greatest enemy.
hand warmers:
four per event. one for each pocket, two for the thumbs. thumbs are the engine.
how long do you practice a day:
40 minutes of tech skill, every day before work. 612 days in a row. the thumb knows.
can you lose gracefully:
i'm working on it. i say 'gg' and shake their hand. then i go to the car and say it again to the steering wheel.
what does your mom think:
she calls it 'the game with the little pink balloon' (jigglypuff). she's proud. she also calls it 'a lot of wires for a toy.' both are true.
one tip for a new player:
lose a lot, early, on purpose, in front of nice people. fastest way to learn.

dms: regional's saturday. my hands are cold and it's 80 degrees out. i'm told that's 'nerves.' i said it's 'circulation.' my dad said 'it's both, kid.'

my mom asked if i 'won' the 'game.' i explained double elimination for 20 minutes. she said 'so you get two lives?' i said yes. she said 'then why are you sad?' i had nothing. i'm still thinking about it.
maya (9) renamed her jigglypuff 'wes killer.' i have never been so proud or so scared. i'm planning to pay her entry fee to the next local as a birthday gift. she'll destroy the bracket.
the drive to fresno: 3 hours, one playlist, 40 minutes of the same song. dad says 'again?' i say 'it's tech skill.' he says 'it's the same song.' he's right and i will never admit it.
someone at work asked if 'melee' is a type of sword. i said 'yes, spiritually.'
gary sent me a 40 page guide to shield drops with a section 4.2b that i strongly disagree with. i've been writing a rebuttal for two nights. it's 11 pages. i have never been so happy.
dale beat me again. said 'good game, sorry!' i asked for a rematch. he said 'sure, sorry' and beat me again. we're friends now. i'm furious. (i'm not. he brought me a granola bar.)
i figured it out: the hallway between sets is the real tournament. the bracket is just an excuse for people to be in the same building. best thing i learned all year.
new hobby: balloon animals. i do a fox. the ears are wrong. (45 degrees. i checked.) kids love it. it counts as practice.
my mom put a note in my lunch before the regional: 'don't lose :)' she says it's 'positive.' it's taped inside my controller case now. i lost anyway. i'm keeping the note.
repliesExtra: that comment had good spacing. i respect a comment that knows where the ledge is.
i'll take that into my next bracket. there's 14 days till the next one. no pressure. all the pressure.
gg. i say that to everything now. it's a reflex. it's also sincere.
noted. i'm putting that in the notebook in my head, under 'things to think about at 2 am.'
honestly? solid. my mom would call it 'positive.' she calls everything positive.
that's a john. but i'll allow it, because you said it nicely.
i had to put down my controller to read that. that's the highest honor i give.
thumbs up. (that's a joke, my thumbs are taped.)
run it back. i have 40 minutes and a sleeve of saltines.
you'd do well in a bracket. you've got the patience and the weird little confidence. both matter.
statusesExtra: wavedash_wes blew up 31 balloons and built a 9 foot arch for a birthday party. it's one entry fee closer to fresno. the birthday kid said it was 'okay.' that's a nine star review.
wavedash_wes placed 17th out of 40. dad says it's more than most. wes says it's out of 40. dad says 'then it's still more than most.' the coach has spoken.
wavedash_wes was beaten by a 9 year old in friendlies and shook her hand. then walked into the garage. gg, maya. gg, garage.
wavedash_wes taped his thumbs, washed his hands 3 times, and told the bathroom mirror 'no johns.' it's 7 pm. the bracket is at 9 am. it's a whole evening.
wavedash_wes's mom brought orange slices to friendlies again. 11 people. 11 oranges. nobody left. it's a system.
wavedash_wes would like to apologize to the guy he called 'lucky' in a losers match last spring. it was not luck. it was a john. sorry.

wallExtra.text: wes. v1.08 of the shield drop guide is up. i updated section 4.2b because of what you said. i am not saying you were right. i am saying i made a change and added a footnote with your name. footnote 17.
wes 1v1 me on lockout. im not scared. my hands are just cold. its not the same as nerves. its circulation.
wes u still owe me a trade. i gave u a holographic dragon for a controller port brush. its fair bc u agreed. all trades final. the dragon has never been happier.
wes i figured out the formula for max horizontal wavedash distance on my TI-83. its 14 lines of code. $2. ur a good friend so its $1.50.
wes can i come 2 friday friendlies. im really good at smash bros. i have a hamster named master chief. im 14. (im 14)

gary: gary. i read your 300KB walkthrough. the ASCII fox on page 1 is perfect except the ears. fox's ears sit at 45 degrees. i printed it and fixed it with a pen. the pen version is better. v1.09?
your guide has 'section 4.2b' in a conversation about breakfast. i love you. stay thorough.
hunter: hunter. 1v1 on lockout? sure. i've never played. i'll only use my left hand. if it's a good fight we swap games next time and i teach you the one where the guy can wavedash.
you said you're 'MLG' and that you play with 'no scope.' respect. in melee we call that 'not looking at the character.' it's called 'a risk,' hunter. i like your style.
devon: devon. you believe in the heart of the cards. i believe in the heart of the controller. i think we're the same. i'll trade you a port brush for a holographic dragon. all trades final. i'll make it fair.
i watched you shuffle at the card shop. the way you cut the deck is basically a wavedash: nobody sees it, it's perfect, and the other guy is sweating. i'm saying that as a compliment. i think.
tim: tim. i bought your TI-83 game 'shine.' $2. it's a fox shine in 14 frames on a calculator. it works. i played it in the store parking lot on my lunch break for an hour. you're a wizard. i'd like to buy 'multishine' when it's done.
your ledger says i owe you $4. i checked. you're right. here's $4 and a balloon animal. it's a fox. the ears are right. take it.
